key_insight: Neural networks can become behaviorally similar on the same task while still carrying distinct internal representations shaped by their earlier training history.
engineering_relevance: For AI-enabled engineering workflows, matching accuracy alone may hide persistent path dependence, so internal-state checks are important when comparing trained models.
method: Paired CNNs start from identical weights and train on tasks in reversed order.
Both models then undergo the same deterministic common-relaxation training distribution.
Controls test longer relaxation, rotated MNIST, and ReLU vs. LeakyReLU effects.
evidence_signal: Across 20 paired MNIST runs, 16 met the behavioral-matching criterion, yet the mean representation-history score remained 0.139 with about 3.1% prediction disagreement; similar persistence held in longer-relaxation and control experiments.
watch_item: The results are protocol-scoped, so the persistence of history effects may depend on the architecture, training schedule, and data regime used.
paper_title: Behavioral Convergence Without Representational Convergence: Persistent Training-History Dependence in Neural Networks
